title: 2004 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: Two-thirds of the people in a room are seated in three-fourths of the chairs. The rest of the people are standing. If there are \(6\) empty chairs, how many people are in the room?

solutions.text:
Since \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the chairs are occupied, the \(6\) empty chairs are \(\frac{1}{4}\) of all the chairs. Thus there are \(24\) chairs.

The number of seated people is \(\frac{3}{4}\) of \(24,\) which is \(18.\)

Those \(18\) seated people are \(\frac{2}{3}\) of all the people, so the total number of people is \(18\div\frac23=27.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The empty chairs are the remaining one-fourth of the chairs.
The seated people are two-thirds of all the people.
